sources.entry: CopyQ - Clipboard manager with advanced features

summary.one_liner: CopyQ is an advanced clipboard manager for Linux, Windows, and macOS 13+ that keeps clipboard history in customizable tabs with editing and scripting features.
summary.what_it_does: CopyQ monitors the system clipboard and saves its content, including text, HTML, images, and other custom formats, into tabs. Saved items can be browsed, filtered, sorted, edited, tagged with notes, repositioned, and pasted back into other applications. It supports system-wide keyboard shortcuts, custom commands that can run from the menu, shortcuts, or when the clipboard changes, and a command-line interface for adding, reading, and copying items. The README also mentions ignoring clipboard content copied from specified windows or containing specified text, and a simple Vim-like editor mode. Items are restored when CopyQ restarts.
use_cases: store and organize copied text or images in tabs
script clipboard actions from the command line
paste previously copied items with keyboard shortcuts
ignore clipboard content from certain apps or text
notable: Command-line and scripting API for controlling the running app
Stores text, HTML, images, and custom clipboard formats
Custom commands bound to shortcuts or clipboard changes
Ignore rules for specific windows or text content
Available via Homebrew, Scoop, Chocolatey, Flatpak, AppImage, and Linux distro packages
caveats: The official Ubuntu PPA is no longer maintained
Command-line control requires the main application to be running
macOS may need manual quarantine removal and codesigning if the app is reported as damaged
